title: Dexcom G6 issues with Android 10 Pixel 4
body:
I tried to run the setup wizard on the G6 and had a lot of issues connecting but after disabling Trust Auto Connect and OB1 Collector I was able to get it to bond. Problem is now I don't think it is utilizing the calibration code and it needs manual calibrations (basically behaves like the G5). Anyway to get the OB1 Collector and Native Mode settings to work on Android 10 so the G6 can function the correct way? Seems to be getting glucose fine for now with manual calibrations.
![Screenshot_20191024-234725](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/56993120/67549454-24e6d100-f6b9-11e9-9d6a-fc9085ea7eb9.png)

comments.body: I am going to use it like this until the sensor stops because with transmitters 81**** once it stops I can't start again. But the issue was that it couldn't bond at all unless OB1 was off. I will try again when I put a new sensor and report back. Thanks for the help.
Confirmed turning off Allow Ob1 Unbonding fixed the issue for me. Xdrip works with the G6 code with no issues now. Thanks for the help.

None of the solutions (involving forgetting the device etc.) helped me, but I did manage to keep my G6 (with a 8G firefly transmitter) running for about a day before I had to forget it again (and restart the collector?). Usually, it didn't pick the sensor back up once it had missed 3-4 readings.

Today, I tried setting Bluetooth AVRCP to version 1.3 in the developer settings of my Pixel 4 XL. Now, it picks my sensor back up after a few missed readings as well as reliably getting readings so far (a few hours).

This isn't the final solution by any means, but I will report back about reliability nevertheless.

Also, if any developer is interested, I can provide logcat output for the connection problems discussed.

Did this work for you? I am a little in over my head since I'm not the most tech savvy but I have tried several different suggestions and not been able to get Xdrip to connect for more than a couple of hours to my G6 since I got the pixel 4. Any input would be helpful!

It does work mostly reliable (random disconnects that don't just connect back after a few readings happen every 5 days or so), but I can't really pinpoint the exact change that breaks xDrip.

To be perfectly honest, I do think that this is probably some battery saving measure that interferes with the repeated BLE connections, quite simply because it got better with time (i.e. some "smart" feature needs some time to pick up on your habits so that it doesn't kill the apps you constantly use). Maybe disabling battery optimization for both xDrip and Bluetooth helped, I don't really know.
